subject: Novamed request: targeted log lifecycle variance and SOC 2 / SIG evidence
messages:
From: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@novamed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@novamed.com
Date: 2025-10-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: targeted log lifecycle variance for novamed-prod and SOC 2/SIG artifacts

Hi Irene,

Quick one from our security and privacy teams — Novamed needs a per-tenant retention variance for one production tenant (namespace: novamed-prod). Our SOC 2 controls require 90 days of session-and-audit-log availability for high-risk clinical workflows; we understand Redwood’s hosted default is 30 days for most inference telemetry.

Could you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Provide a limited, account-scoped retention extension to 90 days for audit/application logs for novamed-prod (we only need audit events, request/response metadata, and delivery traces — not full model KV caches).
- Produce SOC 2 evidence or SIG/CAIQ mappings that show how deletion of tenant logs is executed and how you maintain chain-of-custody for deletions (we need a narrative and any supporting artifact).
- Clarify differences in behavior between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments for this retention change (we are evaluating which to order).

Also please include a timeline to deliver: (1) CAIQ/SIG answers for the Logging & Monitoring and Data Retention sections, and (2) any attestation or change-order language you require so we can present to procurement.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Reynolds
Head of InfoSec Programs, Novamed
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: targeted log lifecycle variance for novamed-prod and SOC 2/SIG artifacts

Team — forwarding Novamed's ask. They want a tenant-scoped 90d retention for audit/application logs, plus SOC2/SIG/CAIQ artifacts showing deletion process and proof-of-delete chain. They explicitly do NOT want KV cache or model checkpoints retained.

Can we confirm the capabilities and a deliverable list? My thoughts:
- Dedicated and Private: we can offer tenant-level retention config or snapshot-based retention; low lift (config + billing amend).
- Hosted: possible but operationally heavier — we'd need an exception path with contract addendum and likely additional storage fees and a rollout window.
- Evidence: security team should prepare CAIQ/SIG answers for Logging & Monitoring + Data Retention, and compliance can produce a short narrative + sample delete log (redaction-safe).

Actions: Karthik — can you confirm technical feasibility and whether we can produce a sanitized proof-of-delete artifact for SOC 2?
Stephanie — can you draft the CAIQ/SIG fragment (Logging/Data Retention) and list what Novamed must sign?
Marissa — please estimate timeline and ops steps to enact a hosted exception vs Dedicated/Private route.

I'll reply to Novamed with a proposed path once we have these.

— Irene
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-08T13:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: targeted log lifecycle variance for novamed-prod and SOC 2/SIG artifacts

Irene / team — technical notes below.

Summary: feasible, with constraints and options.

1) Dedicated / Private
- Per-tenant retention to 90d is straightforward: retention policy is a metadata flag on tenant blobs + log index entries; we keep a TTL on ingestion otherwise. Ops can flip per-tenant retention and backfill if requested (backfill cost).
- We can produce a sanitized proof-of-delete: OIDC-bound deletion job + signed manifest of deleted object keys (with hashes truncated) and retention job audit entries. That artifact satisfies SOC 2 auditors in most cases.

2) Hosted (multi-tenant)
- Hosted default path is 30d. For a hosted exception we can implement a tenant-level override but it requires:
  a) contractual amendment (billing + SLA impact),
  b) a short ops engineering window to add namespace-level retention exceptions to the runtime (2–3 weeks), and
  c) limited escalation around snapshot/backfill if they want historic logs preserved.
- We must not expose model KV cache retention — we'll enforce a policy to continue pruning ephemeral caches at 30d.

3) Artifacts we can deliver (examples attached):
- retention_matrix_v1.xlsx — maps log type (audit, request metadata, debug traces, kv-cache) to retention, deletion method, and proof artifact.
- redwood_caiq_answers_oct2025.pdf — CAIQ fragment for Logging & Retention controls (we can redact environment-specific ids).
- sample_signed_delete_manifest.txt (generated by ops) — contains timestamps, truncated object hashes, and operator IDs.

Constraints / notes:
- For hosted exceptions, we will require an indemnity carveout for extended retention and a cost premium.
- We should limit scope to audit + request metadata; client-visible request/response payloads may raise data classification questions.

I'll produce a short technical note and the sample manifest. Ops will need Marissa's go-ahead for any backfill.

— Karthik
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Reynolds <sam.reynolds@novamed.com>
Cc: compliance@novamed.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-09T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: targeted log lifecycle variance for novamed-prod and SOC 2/SIG artifacts

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask and patience while we scoped this. Summary and next steps below.

What we can offer
- Dedicated or Private deployment: we can configure account-scoped retention to 90 days for audit logs and request/response metadata for namespace novamed-prod. KV cache and model artifacts will continue to follow the 30-day ephemeral policy.
- Hosted: we can support a hosted exception but it requires a contractual amendment (billing delta + ops window). We will need a signed amendment before we flip the flag in production.

Deliverables (target dates)
- CAIQ/SIG fragment for Logging & Data Retention — attached (redwood_caiq_answers_oct2025.pdf). Delivery: today.
- Retention matrix mapping log types to deletion method and proof artifacts — attached (retention_matrix_v1.xlsx). Delivery: today.
- Sample signed delete manifest (sanitized) and deletion narrative suitable for auditors — can deliver by 2025-10-15.
- Draft change-order language for hosted exceptions / Dedicated upgrade (fee schedule + SLAs) — will share 2025-10-12 (novamed_variance_draft_amendment.docx).

Conditions and recommended path
- If Novamed plans to remain on Redwood Hosted, we recommend the contract amendment + a 2–3 week ops schedule to implement the override and run any required backfill.
- If you choose Dedicated or Private, we can enable the 90d retention at activation with lower operational risk and no backfill fee.
- We will only include audit and request metadata in the extended retention by default; if you need payloads, we need info classification approval and possibly encryption-at-rest exceptions.

Please confirm which path you prefer (Hosted with amendment vs Dedicated/Private) and whether Novamed legal would like the draft amendment for review. Once we have a confirmation, we’ll queue the artifacts and provide a fixed delivery schedule.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_caiq_answers_oct2025.pdf (PDF, 22 pages, CAIQ fragment), retention_matrix_v1.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet), novamed_variance_draft_amendment.docx (Word, 3 pages)
